Entry: The entry point tells Webpack where to start resolving dependencies. It's the root module that Webpack uses to build the dependency graph.
Output: Output configuration tells Webpack where to emit the bundled files and how to name them. The path and filename properties are required.
Loaders: Loaders allow Webpack to process files other than JavaScript by transforming them into valid modules. They are defined in the module.rules array.
Plugins: Plugins extend Webpack's capabilities by performing optimizations, asset management, and environment injection. They are added to the plugins array.

const HtmlWebpackPlugin = require('html-webpack-plugin');
module.exports = { plugins: [new HtmlWebpackPlugin({ template: './src/index.html' })] };

Babel: Babel transpiles modern ES6+ JavaScript into backwards-compatible versions. The @babel/preset-env preset handles syntax transformation based on target browsers.
module.exports = { module: { rules: [{ test: /\.js$/, exclude: /node_modules/, use: { loader: 'babel-loader', options: { presets: ['@babel/preset-env'] } } }] } };
CSS/SASS: CSS and SASS loaders transform stylesheets into JavaScript modules. The chain of loaders processes right-to-left, typically sass-loader -> css-loader -> style-loader.
Images: Asset modules allow importing images as base64-encoded strings or separate files. The type: 'asset' setting automatically chooses between inline and file output.
Fonts: Font files can be processed using asset modules or file-loader. They are typically emitted as separate files with hashed filenames for caching.

HtmlWebpack: HtmlWebpackPlugin simplifies creation of HTML files that automatically include all Webpack bundles. It supports templating and minification.

const HtmlWebpackPlugin = require('html-webpack-plugin');
module.exports = { plugins: [new HtmlWebpackPlugin({ title: 'My App', template: './src/index.html' })] };
MiniCssExtract: MiniCssExtractPlugin extracts CSS into separate files instead of inlining them in JavaScript. This improves caching and parallel loading.

const MiniCssExtractPlugin = require('mini-css-extract-plugin');
module.exports = { module: { rules: [{ test: /\.css$/, use: [MiniCssExtractPlugin.loader, 'css-loader'] }] }, plugins: [new MiniCssExtractPlugin()] };
DefinePlugin: DefinePlugin creates global constants at compile time, useful for injecting environment variables. Values are evaluated as code expressions.

Code Splitting: Code splitting breaks bundles into smaller chunks loaded on demand, reducing initial load time. SplitChunksPlugin handles shared module extraction.
module.exports = { optimization: { splitChunks: { chunks: 'all', cacheGroups: { vendor: { test: /[\\/]node_modules[\\/]/, name: 'vendors' } } } } };
Tree Shaking: Tree shaking eliminates dead code by analyzing ES module import/export statements. It requires 'sideEffects': false in package.json and production mode.
Minification: TerserWebpackPlugin minifies JavaScript by removing whitespace, renaming variables, and eliminating dead code. It runs automatically in production mode.

const TerserPlugin = require('terser-webpack-plugin');
module.exports = { optimization: { minimizer: [new TerserPlugin({ extractComments: false })] } };

Dev/Prod: Separate Webpack configs for development and production allow different optimizations. A common config merged via webpack-merge avoids duplication.

const { merge } = require('webpack-merge');
module.exports = (env) => merge(commonConfig, env.prod ? prodConfig : devConfig);
Multiple Configs: Webpack supports exporting an array of configurations for building multiple bundles in a single run, useful for libraries or multi-page apps.
module.exports = [{ entry: './a.js', output: { filename: 'a.js' } }, { entry: './b.js', output: { filename: 'b.js' } }];
Env Variables: Environment variables can be passed via CLI using --env and accessed in the config function. DefinePlugin injects them into application code.

HMR: Hot Module Replacement updates modules in the browser without a full page reload. It preserves application state during development.
module.exports = { devServer: { hot: true }, plugins: [new webpack.HotModuleReplacementPlugin()] };
Proxy: Dev server proxy forwards API requests to a backend server during development, avoiding CORS issues. It supports path rewriting and HTTPS.
Live Reload: Live reload automatically refreshes the browser when files change. It is enabled by default in webpack-dev-server and works with watch mode.
module.exports = { watch: true, devServer: { liveReload: true } };

Module Federation: Module Federation allows multiple separate Webpack builds to share code and components at runtime. It enables micro-frontend architectures.
new ModuleFederationPlugin({ name: 'app1', remotes: { app2: 'app2@http://localhost:3002/remoteEntry.js' }, shared: { react: { singleton: true } } })
Custom Loaders: Custom loaders transform source files by implementing a function that receives the source and returns the modified output. Loaders run in a pipeline.
Custom Plugins: Custom plugins hook into Webpack's compilation lifecycle using the apply method and tap into compiler hooks for custom behavior.
class MyPlugin { apply(compiler) { compiler.hooks.emit.tapAsync('MyPlugin', (compilation, cb) => { cb(); }); } }

Bundle Analysis: Bundle analysis tools visualize the composition of output bundles, helping identify large dependencies and opportunities for code splitting.
Caching: Webpack uses content hashes in filenames to enable long-term caching. The [contenthash] placeholder generates unique hashes based on file contents.
Long-term Caching: Long-term caching strategies separate vendor code from application code so vendors change less frequently. Module IDs should be deterministic.

module.exports = { optimization: { moduleIds: 'deterministic', runtimeChunk: 'single', splitChunks: { cacheGroups: { vendor: { test: /[\\/]node_modules[\\/]/, name: 'vendors', chunks: 'all' } } } } };
